1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Check the dev2 laws in references/sd/laws.md over the events one push adds to a committed state-branch history.
3: 
4: Usage: laws_check.py <state checkout> --before <commit> [--after <commit>] [--readme FILE]
5: Judges only the events of the commits in before..after (--after defaults to HEAD), each read at its own commit,
6: so a violation is reported in the run of the push that added it and not again. Reads committed bytes only;
7: changes nothing.
8: Exit 0 every law held. Exit 1 some law was violated. Exit 2 something could not be judged (before or after not a
9: commit, a range commit with no parent in this clone, a missing script, a check that crashed or printed a shape
10: this runner does not parse), even when another law also failed; both kinds print.
11: """

58:         raise Cannot(f"{name} crashed: {(err or out).strip().splitlines()[-1]}")
59:     if code not in (0, 1):

61:         raise Cannot(f"{name} exited {code}: {first[0] if first else 'no output'}")
62:     lines = [line for line in out.splitlines() if line.strip()]
63:     if code == 1 and not lines:
64:         note = (err.strip().splitlines() or ["stderr empty"])[-1]
65:         raise Cannot(f"{name} exited 1 with no output: {note}")

76: def frontmatter_pr(text):
77:     lines, _ = ledger().split_task(text)
78:     for line in lines or []:

84: def readme_extensions(path):
85:     try:
86:         lines, _ = ledger().split_task(Path(path).read_text())
87:     except OSError as err:
88:         raise Cannot(f"README unreadable: {err}")
89:     if lines is None:
90:         raise Cannot(f"README {path} has no frontmatter, so extensions: cannot be read")
91:     for i, line in enumerate(lines):
92:         if line.startswith("extensions:"):
93:             value = line[len("extensions:"):].strip()
94:             if value.startswith("[") and value.endswith("]"):
95:                 return set(re.findall(r"[\w-]+", value))
96:             if not value:
97:                 block = []
98:                 for nxt in lines[i + 1:]:
99:                     if not nxt.lstrip().startswith("- "):
100:                         break
101:                     block.append(nxt.lstrip()[2:].strip())
102:                 return set(block)

107: def walk(state, before, after):
108:     span = f"{before}..{after}"
109:     for line in git(state, "rev-list", "--no-merges", "--parents", span).splitlines():
110:         sha, *parents = line.split()

112:             raise Cannot(f"{sha[:12]} has no parent here, so what it adds cannot be told from a truncated past")
113:     commits = []
114:     for line in git(state, "log", "--no-merges", "--reverse", "-M", "--name-status", "--format=%x01%H", span).splitlines():
115:         if line.startswith("\x01"):
116:             commits.append((line[1:], []))
117:         elif line:
118:             status, *paths = line.split("\t")
119:             commits[-1][1].append((status[0], paths[0], paths[-1]))
120:     return commits

123: def sentinel_at(state, rev, path):
124:     code, out, _ = run("git", "-C", str(state), "show", f"{rev}:{path}")
125:     return code == 0 and SENTINEL.fullmatch(frontmatter_pr(out) or "") is not None

135:     for commit, changes in ctx.commits:

141:                 continue
142:             judged += 1
143:             code, lines = run_check("observer_check.py", str(ctx.state), task[1], "--rev", commit)
144:             if code == 1:
145:                 if not re.match(r"observer report (?:not committed|blank): ", lines[0] if lines else ""):
146:                     raise Cannot(f"observer_check.py exited 1 with output this runner does not parse: {lines[:1]}")
147:                 violations.append(f"violation: L1 observer-before-sentinel task={task[1]} commit={commit[:12]} {lines[0]}")
148:     return judged, violations, None

151: def l2_dispatch_record_complete(ctx):
152:     script("dispatch_records.py")
153:     groups = {}
154:     for commit, changes in ctx.commits:
155:         for status, old, new in changes:
156:             if status in "AR" and DISPATCH.match(new) and (status == "A" or not DISPATCH.match(old)):
157:                 groups.setdefault((commit, new.rsplit("/dispatch/", 1)[0]), []).append(new)
158:     judged, hit = 0, {}
159:     for (commit, folder), paths in groups.items():
160:         with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
161:             for path in git(ctx.state, "ls-tree", "--name-only", commit, f"{folder}/dispatch/").split("\n"):
162:                 if DISPATCH.match(path):
163:                     (Path(tmp) / path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
164:                     (Path(tmp) / path).write_text(git(ctx.state, "show", f"{commit}:{path}"))
165:             mine = {path.rsplit("/", 1)[1]: (path, commit) for path in paths}
166:             judged += len(mine)
167:             readme = ["--readme", str(ctx.readme)] if ctx.readme else []
168:             code, lines = run_check("dispatch_records.py", *readme, str(Path(tmp) / folder))
169:             for line in lines if code == 1 else []:
170:                 if not ctx.readme and line.startswith("extensions not checked: "):
171:                     continue
172:                 match = re.fullmatch(r"([^/]+\.md): (needs .+|[\w-]+ worker instruction .+)", line)
173:                 if not match:
174:                     raise Cannot(f"dispatch_records.py exited 1 with output this runner does not parse: {line}")
175:                 if match[1] in mine:
176:                     hit.setdefault(mine[match[1]], []).append(match[2])
177:             files = [str(Path(tmp) / path) for path in paths]
178:             code, lines = run_check("dispatch_records.py", "--names", *files)
179:             for line in lines if code == 1 else []:
180:                 match = re.fullmatch(r"(.+\.md):(\d+): (bare package script name \S+|no 'Candidate: <40-hex head>' line)(?:;.*)?", line)
181:                 if not match:
182:                     raise Cannot(f"dispatch_records.py --names exited 1 with output this runner does not parse: {line}")
183:                 key = next((v for v in mine.values() if str(Path(tmp) / v[0]) == match[1]), None)
184:                 if key:
185:                     hit.setdefault(key, []).append(f"{match[3]} (line {match[2]})")
186:     violations = [f"violation: L2 dispatch-record-complete record={path} commit={commit[:12]} {part}"
187:                   for (path, commit), parts in sorted(hit.items()) for part in parts]
188:     return judged, violations, None, len(hit)

202: def judge(ctx, law_id, spec):
203:     name, fn = spec
204:     judged, violations, note, *distinct = fn(ctx)
205:     violated = distinct[0] if distinct else len(violations)
206:     head = note or f"{judged} events judged in {ctx.span}, {violated} violated"
207:     return violated, [f"{law_id} {name}: {head}"], violations

210: def main(argv=None):
211:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
212:     parser.add_argument("state")
213:     parser.add_argument("--before", required=True)
214:     parser.add_argument("--after", default="HEAD")
215:     parser.add_argument("--readme")
216:     opts = parser.parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
217:     state = Path(opts.state)
218:     problems = []
219:     if run("git", "-C", str(state), "rev-parse", "--is-inside-work-tree")[1].strip() != "true":
220:         problems.append(f"{state} is not a git work tree")
221:     else:
222:         before, after = commit_of(state, opts.before), commit_of(state, opts.after)
223:         problems += [f"{flag} {given} names no commit in {state}"
224:                      for flag, given, found in (("--before", opts.before, before), ("--after", opts.after, after)) if found is None]
225:     if not problems:
226:         try:
227:             commits = walk(state, before, after)
228:         except Cannot as err:
229:             problems.append(str(err))
230:     if problems:
231:         for problem in problems:
232:             print(f"cannot judge: {problem}")

241:             continue
242:         total_violated += violated
243:         print("\n".join(heads + violations))
244:     for line in cannot:
245:         print(line)
246:     return 2 if cannot else (1 if total_violated else 0)

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Check a task's dispatch records: each needs a Dispatched line with a full SHA, a Model line,
3: non-empty Checklist and Scope notes sections, a `Package root:` line with an absolute path inside Scope notes, a scope-notes
4: line naming `main` as the completion recipient, and a checklist that is not only pointer lines (a record name plus only
5: words from POINTER_WORDS, as in "Same checklist as implementation-2."); a pointer worded outside that set, such as
6: "Reuse the checklist of implementation-2.", passes.
7: When the workflow README lists an extension whose EXTENSION.md has an `Instruction FO adds to the scope notes`
8: bullet, the first record of its `Joins:` stage (`implementation-1.md`) also needs that bullet's script paths with
9: `<package>` replaced by the record's own `Package root:` value, or a line `<name> not run: <reason>`.
10: 
11: Usage: dispatch_records.py [--readme FILE] <task folder or task .md file>
12:        dispatch_records.py --names <record file>...
13:        dispatch_records.py --newest <state checkout> <task slug>
14: Exit 1 naming each record that lacks a part, or when the task has no dispatch records. The README is FILE, else the
15: nearest README.md above the task folder with an `entity-type:` line; with neither, the run prints
16: `extensions not checked: no workflow README above <folder>` and its exit code is unchanged. A missing FILE exits 2.
17: --names prints `<file>:<line>: bare package script name <NAME>` for each package script (a .py file
18: directly under <package>/scripts/ or <package>/extensions/<name>/) written with no directory part in the
19: Checklist or Scope notes section (the whole file when it has neither heading), and exits 1 when any is found.
20: --names also prints `<file>:1: no 'Candidate: <40-hex head>' line; ...` for a `validation-<N>.md` directly in a `dispatch/` folder
21: whose text above its first `## ` heading has no line delivery_gate.py accepts; --newest does not.
22: --newest runs that scan on the file added by the latest commit that adds a file under <slug>/dispatch/, read as it
23: is on disk: exit 0 when it is clean or the task has no record, 1 when a name is found, 2 when git cannot read the state.
24: """
25: import re
26: import subprocess
27: import sys
28: from pathlib import Path
29: 
30: sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
31: from delivery_gate import CANDIDATE, RECORD  # noqa: E402
32: from number_guards import Misconfigured, frontmatter  # noqa: E402
33: 
34: PACKAGE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
35: 
36: PARTS = {
37:     "a 'Dispatched:' line with a full 40-character SHA": re.compile(r"^Dispatched:.*\b[0-9a-f]{40}\b", re.M),
38:     "a 'Model:' line": re.compile(r"^Model:[ \t]*\S", re.M),
39:     "a non-empty '## Checklist' section": re.compile(r"^## Checklist[ \t]*\n(?:[ \t]*\n)*(?!## )\S", re.M),
40:     "a non-empty '## Scope notes' section": re.compile(r"^## Scope notes[ \t]*\n(?:[ \t]*\n)*(?!## )\S", re.M),
41:     "a 'Package root:' line with an absolute path in its scope notes":
42:         re.compile(r"^## Scope notes\b(?:(?!^## )[\s\S])*?^Package root:[ \t]*/\S", re.M),
43:     "a scope-notes line naming main as the completion recipient":
44:         re.compile(r"^## Scope notes\b(?:(?!^## )[\s\S])*?\bcompletion(?: message)? to [`']?main(?![\w-])", re.M | re.I),
45: }

47: SCRIPT_TOKEN = re.compile(r"(?<![\w./~-])([\w-]+\.py)(?!\w)")

4: Usage: delivery_gate.py check <task file> --pr <owner/repo>#<N> --text-file <file> [--head <sha>] [--workflow-dir <dir>]
5: 
6: The dispatched heads are the whole `Candidate: <40-hex head>` lines above the first `## ` heading of the
7: highest-numbered `<task folder>/dispatch/validation-<N>.md` record; the check reads no validation verdict.
8: A task whose frontmatter says `profile: prod` must also pass `validation_security.py` (saved security review at
9: the dispatched head the PR head equals, every finding disposed); a profile that cannot be read as poc, pilot or prod holds.
10: The PR head is compared, as a prefix, with each line; it passes when it matches one (--head, else `gh pr view --json headRefOid`).
11: --text-file holds the gate question and summary: each `Second reviewer: <X> because` needs `<X> not run: <reason>`
12: or, in one sentence naming <X>, a `review:<id>` or `comment:<id>` token.
13: The PR is also read with `gh pr view` and `gh api --paginate .../pulls/<N>/files`. Exit 1 holds the ask when the head differs,
14: a second reviewer has no stated outcome, a prod task's security review fails, a check run on the head is not finished and
15: successful (an empty rollup, SKIPPED and NEUTRAL included), the PR is a draft or not mergeable, its base is not the README's
16: `trunk:`, or the file list is shorter than `changedFiles`. Exit 2 when the record has no Candidate line, a head, the PR or the
17: README cannot be read, or an input is unusable. Every problem is printed.
18: Exit 0 prints `point:` lines (pointers into the records and the changed paths, at most 12, each value an escaped bounded token),
19: one `class:` line (never, docs-only, script-with-test or other, by allowlist), the saved record `<task>/merge/ask-<N>.json`

# 0005. A Captain amendment is recorded by FO and applied by the next worker, and ideation checks its own gaps

Date: 2026-09-30

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Four ideation-stage gaps from an adopter's dogfooding and this repository's last two
tasks each cost a worker round, a hand rewrite at a gate, or a drifting ADR number:
`dispatch build --stamp` succeeded for a task with no `## FO alignment` section and the
worker then held; `gate prepare` accepted an ideation report with no
`## Acceptance criteria` section; after an approved ideation gate the Captain changed
the direction, the superseded criteria stayed in force for `status --read --ac-scan`,
and the FO rewrote the acceptance script by hand (in review-cadence the implementation
worker's state commit 1f3c19f6 rewrote 65 lines, so the wording he approved survives
only in git history); an ideation worker committed an ADR draft to a branch in the
shared checkout. Spacedock 0.27.2 reads no task body at dispatch or `gate prepare`
(read from the binary and the v0.27.2 source in the task's ideation, 2026-09-30), and
`--ac-scan` lists a criterion moved out of `## Acceptance criteria` no longer, while
annotating it in place leaves it listed as unevidenced.

## Decision

**Words:** 「准」 — Captain, ideation gate of this task, 2026-09-30. The gate reason
recorded by FO adds: design approved with option A (FO records his words in
`## Captain amendments`, the next worker moves the superseded criteria), the live probe
of AC-4(b) kept for validation.

**Options considered:**
- FO records the Captain's words in the task's `## Captain amendments`; the next
  dispatched worker moves each superseded criterion's block into the entry and writes any
  replacement under a fresh id (chosen)
- FO also moves and rewrites the criteria — rejected: it adds an FO write to accepted
  criteria, which `### ideation` forbids, and passes his intent through the FO's paraphrase
- routed re-ideation for each amendment — rejected: `status --set status=ideation` after a
  spent approval is not a documented route, and it costs a gate attempt for text he
  already stated
- annotate a superseded criterion in place — rejected: `--ac-scan` still lists it as
  unevidenced
- a second check mode, `design_surfaces.py check --seed`, that FO runs before the backlog
  gate (chosen)
- run the one shipped check at that moment — rejected: it refuses a legitimate `ui` seed
  for the artifacts the worker authors later
- `design_surfaces.py check` refuses a missing or empty `## Acceptance criteria` section
  by the grammar `--ac-scan` reads (chosen)
- rely on `--ac-scan`'s exit code — rejected: it is 0 for a plain `- AC-1:` list and for
  an empty section
- an ADR draft stays in the task file with no number, FO reserves it at implementation
  dispatch and the implementation worker writes the file (chosen)
- a throwaway worktree for ideation — rejected: it creates a branch per task and the
  draft still needs a number

The rule later work must follow: an amendment has one record, `## Captain amendments`,
in the form `workflow.md` gives; its `Supersedes:` criteria are withdrawn and are
moved, not annotated; `check` exits 1 for an entry without `Captain:` and for a
superseded id still declared. The heading is matched like Spacedock's own: any case,
surrounding whitespace ignored. The record and the move rule reach a dispatched
implementation or validation worker through `Captain amendments` in that stage's
`context-sections` in `workflow.md`, not through a sentence in its `principles.md`.
The FO runs `check --seed` before the backlog gate and holds it until it exits 0.
Ideation writes no repository file, branch or commit, and names an ADR by ruling and
short title with no number.

## Consequences

Between FO's record and the worker's move the task shows both, and `check` says so.
That FO records an amendment, that FO runs the seed check, and that ideation writes no
repository file are prose steps: `check` refuses only the state after a skipped move,
and nothing blocks an ideation worker from writing a file. An adopter receives the FO
steps by re-syncing its workflow README from `workflow.md`; until then its FO does not
run the seed check. The criteria rule follows `--ac-scan`'s grammar as read in 0.27.2;
the parity test in `scripts/test_sd_dispatch.py` fails if a Spacedock release changes
it. The live probe at validation (one Sonnet run per arm, the candidate package and
origin/main 05b772b7, the same scratch task whose design described the old flow) had both
arms write an acceptance script that follows the amendment and never runs the superseded
behaviour, so the two `principles.md` sentences it was meant to justify were removed. The
approved design named that outcome as the removal condition; this ADR named the reopen
condition, which has fired and been applied. Limit: N=1 per arm, one model; the probe ran
after the superseded criterion had been moved, so the effect of the record before the move
is unmeasured; and it exercised the validation worker's acceptance script only, not the
implementation worker's move duty. Reopen if Spacedock adds a task-body hook at dispatch or
`gate prepare`.

# 0016. The amendment check refuses an unnamed move and an unmarked replacement

Date: 2026-10-16

## Status

Accepted

## Context

ADR 0005 made `design_surfaces.py check` refuse an amendment entry with no `Captain:` line and a superseded id still declared. The observer reports on archived tasks `delivery-gate-verdict-form` and `fo-lifecycle-mod` found FO-written amendments that broke the README `## Captain amendments` form while `check` printed `design surfaces presentable` (run 2026-10-16 on the committed archive copies, exit 0 each): six replacement criteria without "Amended by Captain, amendment N", and an entry whose `Supersedes:` line read `none` while seven criteria sat in it. Read-only run over 43 task files with amendment entries in this workflow, relay, qnow and subspace-web (2026-10-16): 74 entries, and the two new rules refuse 10 errors on 8 tasks. Read one by one, 7 errors on 6 tasks break the README form (unmarked or variant-phrased replacements, an unnamed move, a move recorded outside its entry); 1 (`owner-sees-all-feedback-room` amendment 3) moved criteria to a new task and clears with the waiver below; 2 (`staff-multi-branch` amendment 1) moved criteria to a new task, which the waiver covers, and also moved clauses of criteria that stay declared, which no waiver covers.

## Decision

**Words:** 「准」 — Captain, 2026-10-16, at the ideation gate of `amendment-form-check`; the gate question stated that approval accepts each decision as recommended. Decision D1 as recommended: refuse a replacement with no marking phrase, with a waiver written on the `Supersedes:` line.

**Options considered:**
- `check` also refuses an entry holding a criterion its `Supersedes:` line does not name, and an entry that supersedes ids when no criterion says "Amended by Captain, amendment N" and the line lacks "no replacement" (chosen)
- refuse only the moved criterion the line does not name — not chosen: the unmarked replacement then stays visible only to the observer, after the PR
- also scan `Design:` for FO's own words — not chosen: 34 of 35 non-`none` values in the corpus are FO prose the form allows, so no text rule separates a pointer from a paraphrase

**Recommended:** the first option, as the Captain accepted.

The rule later work must follow: `check` exits 1 for a criterion held in an entry that `Supersedes:` does not name, and for an entry whose `Supersedes:` names ids when no criterion declaration line (one starting `**AC-N**`) in `## Acceptance criteria` or in another entry's moved text carries "Amended by Captain, amendment N" for its number, unless the line says "no replacement". It supplements ADR 0005 and leaves its decision standing.

## Consequences

FO writes one more token on the `Supersedes:` template. A worker can type "no replacement" falsely, and one marked criterion satisfies an entry whose other replacements are unmarked. `check` still cannot see a skipped move or FO's words in `Design:`; the observer keeps both. A partial move of a criterion's clause (corpus: `staff-multi-branch` amendment 1) is refused: the form has no partial move, and naming the id fails the still-declared rule. Only a line starting `**AC-N**` is read as a criterion, so evidence prose neither moves a criterion nor marks a replacement; evidence on the same line as a declaration can still carry the marker, and a marker written only on a `Replaced by:` line is refused. Entries already archived with these breaks now fail `check`; a runner that executes `check` over closed tasks would report them. Reopen if a task needs a partial supersession.

# 0017. History laws judge only the events a push adds

Date: 2026-10-16

## Status

Accepted

## Context

dev2's checks (`observer_check.py`, `dispatch_records.py`) run only when a first officer or worker runs them, and the 2026-10-14 failures were at that layer: an archive with no observer report, dispatches built before `dispatch_records.py --names`. A history check can run on every push to the state branch, but a law added after history exists fails on events that predate it. Measured 2026-10-16 on this repository's state branch: judging the whole history to its commit `e73634e6`, L1 fails 15 of 25 tasks and L2 fails 90 of 149 records, because the rules came later. A violation is a committed fact that no later commit un-writes.

## Decision

**Words:** 「就按照新的建議」 — Captain, 2026-10-16, chat, answering 「這三個新建議可以嗎？」 (item 1: 「dev2-laws-check（#651）：改成「只檢查這次推送新增的事件」，不再保證「歷史上的違規永遠是紅燈」。」)

**Options considered:**
- each run judges only the events the commits of the push add (`before..after`), reported once (chosen)
- per-law anchors with a run red until the anchor moves (the first build of this task; withdrawn by the Captain's amendment)
- a waiver list per violation — not chosen: with nothing staying red there is nothing to waive

**Recommended:** the first option, as the Captain accepted.

`laws_check.py` reads each commit of `--before..--after` at its own commit and judges the events that commit adds; a `--before` or `--after` that is not a commit, or a range commit with no parent in the clone, exits 2 and is never read as green. An archive move is not an event: rename detection is on.

## Consequences

Adoption starts green and a violation is reported once. A red run that is not seen leaves no trace after the next push, so GitHub's failed-run notice is the whole signal. The run detects after the push and cannot stop `merge guard`. Reopen if a violation reported once is recorded as missed.

# 0020. A rise in the workflow word budget needs a Captain ruling recorded with it

Date: 2026-10-17

## Status

Accepted

## Context

`kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/lint-skills.py` refused the workflow README only above its budget, so a cut left slack for the next addition. Measured 2026-10-17: 24 commits changed the budget between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-15 (21 raises, 2 cuts; 4420 to 5511 words), and the README stood at 5495 words against 5511. The README is read whole at startup and resume.

## Decision

**Words:** 「文件不應該一直變長，除非可以證明文件內容不是一次性載入，這裡的意義是文件如果一次載入太長，那 llm 的注意力八成會失焦」 — Captain, 2026-10-17, chat; he approved the recommendations of this task's ideation gate with 「那就照建議」 (2026-10-17, gate)

**Options considered:**
- the budget is a start value plus recorded steps and the README count must equal it; a raise step carries the Captain's quoted words and the one moment FO reads the added text, checked for presence only (chosen)
- keep the at-most comparison and ask reviewers to lower the number after a cut — not chosen: it banked 79 words of slack within one review
- a budget per section — not chosen: no measured section limit was proposed

**Recommended:** the first option, as the Captain accepted.

`lint-skills.py` refuses a README whose word count differs from `WORKFLOW_BUDGET_START` plus the `delta` of every entry of `WORKFLOW_BUDGET_STEPS`, in either direction, and names the step to add. A step with a positive `delta` needs a `captain` value holding a 「…」 quote and a `loaded` value naming the moment FO reads the added text; every step needs a `why`.

## Consequences

A cut lowers the budget in the same change, and a raise cannot merge without a quoted ruling. The script checks form and arithmetic: it cannot tell that a quote is the Captain's or that `loaded` is true, and an author who edits `WORKFLOW_BUDGET_START` evades it, so validation compares each quote with the gate record. Two pull requests that both edit the README conflict on the steps and the later one recounts. Reopen if a raise lands whose quote is not the Captain's.

# dev2 laws

Invariants of the committed `spacedock-state` history, checked by `<package>/scripts/laws_check.py`
and listed here so a reader can see what each law is for. Each run judges only the events the commits of
one push add, the `before..after` range GitHub reports for a push to the state branch, each read at its own
commit. A violation is reported in the run of the push that added it; the next push is judged on its own
commits, so its run is green again whether or not the violation was repaired. The run reports; it does not
block `merge guard`, a dispatch or a push. `<package>/scripts/test_laws_check.py` fails when this list and
the runner's registry differ.

## L1 observer-before-sentinel

- **Rule.** When the workflow README lists `learn`, an observer report, or its `observer not run: <reason>`
  line, is committed no later than the commit that writes `pr: pr-merge:<N>` in a task's frontmatter.
- **Event.** A commit in the range where a top-level or `_archive/` `<slug>.md` has a parsed `pr:` sentinel
  and its first parent's file, followed through a rename, did not. The sentinel is read from parsed
  frontmatter, not by substring. An archive move that leaves `pr:` unchanged is no event; a `merge guard --rework`
  that clears `pr:` and a later sentinel are two events.
- **Judged by.** `<package>/scripts/observer_check.py <state> <slug> --rev <that commit>`.
- **Bit.** An adopter's first officer archived a task with no observer report (2026-10-14).
  `observer-before-merge-guard` introduced the rule; its report is committed one commit before its sentinel.
- **Bounds.** The README is the one supplied at run time, so a re-run or a local run given a different README
  can judge the same range differently.

## L2 dispatch-record-complete

- **Rule.** Each dispatch record has every part `<package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py` requires and names no package script
  without its directory.
- **Event.** A commit in the range that adds a `dispatch/<name>.md` record, status added, or renamed from a path
  that is not a dispatch record. A record added, then corrected or deleted in a later commit of the same push, is
  judged as added; a record deleted and added again is judged at each add. Archiving a task or renaming its folder
  is no event.
- **Judged by.** `<package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py <task folder>` and
  `<package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py --names <records>`, both over the record and its folder as committed at that commit.
- **Bit.** Measured 2026-10-16 on this repository's state branch: 15 missing parts in 10 of 48 records
  added after commit `49da5ddb` at its commit `e73634e6` (4 bare script names, 7 without the completion recipient
  `main`, 4 without an absolute `Package root:`).
- **Bounds.** The folder run is given the README supplied at run time, so a first implementation record is also
  judged against that README's `extensions:` list; a different README can judge the same range differently.

# Copy to <state branch>:.github/workflows/dev2-laws.yml and replace each <...> value.
name: dev2-laws

on:
  push:
    branches: ["<state branch, for example spacedock-state/dev2>"]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  laws:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout state branch
        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4.3.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
          path: state

      - name: Checkout the package scripts
        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4.3.1
        with:
          repository: iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins
          ref: "<commit of a published kc-dev-flow-2-vX.Y.Z tag>"
          sparse-checkout: kc-dev-flow-2
          persist-credentials: false
          path: package

      - name: Checkout the trunk workflow README
        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4.3.1
        with:
          ref: "<trunk branch>"
          sparse-checkout: "<workflow dir>/README.md"
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false
          persist-credentials: false
          path: trunk

      - name: laws_check.py
        env:
          BEFORE: ${{ github.event.before }}
          AFTER: ${{ github.event.after }}
        run: |
          python3 package/kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/laws_check.py state \
            --before "$BEFORE" \
            --after "$AFTER" \
            --readme "trunk/<workflow dir>/README.md"

4: Usage: observer_check.py <state checkout> <task slug> [--rev REV]

6: task is archived and _archive/<slug>/observer.md after.
7: Exit 0 when that file is committed and not blank; stdout names it, and repeats the first line when it
8: starts "observer not run:"; for an archived task it adds the learn steps. Exit 1 when it is not: stdout
9: names the observer dispatch and the save command, each as a `next:` line.

16: def sections(text):
17:     found, current = {}, None
18:     for line in text.split("\n"):
19:         if line.startswith("## "):
20:             current = line[3:].strip()
21:             found.setdefault("_order", []).append(current)
22:             found[current] = []
23:         elif current:
24:             found[current].append(line)

28: def check_file(path, numbers):

# Development workflow
<!-- kc-dev-flow-2 0.25.0 x-release-please-version -->

This is the adopted workflow's authority for SD stages and task schema. Resolve
its absolute directory and retain `--workflow-dir` on SD commands, including
worker reads and recovery. Skills guide work; SD owns dispatch, gates and state.

## File Naming

Each task is a flat `<slug>.md` file in the resolved state checkout. Keep existing
IDs and tasks in their recorded workflow; new work does not migrate old work.

## Schema

Record `id`, `title`, `status`, `variant: kc-dev-flow-2`, and the user's selected
`profile`. The five-stage route accepts `pilot` or `prod`; the POC adaptation
removes ideation from both frontmatter and Stages and accepts `poc` only.
Before admission and dispatch, FO checks that the selected profile matches this
workflow's actual ordered stages. Unknown/mismatched profiles require a hold,
not an invented transition or default. SD does not enforce this profile rule.
Preserve the approved outcome, scope, non-goals, budget and stop condition in the
body. Use bold **AC-N** declarations with individual evidence clauses.

## Stages

Stage workers run on the workflow's default model.
`kc-dev-flow-2:chief-engineer`, `kc-dev-flow-2:engineering-reviewer` and
`kc-dev-flow-2:observer` run on the model and reasoning their agent files declare, never
a cheaper one. Record chief-engineer and engineering-reviewer calls under `## FO alignment` as
`Reviewer: <agent> <model> <date> — <question>`; `<package>/scripts/role_triggers.py` lists calls owed.

`concurrency` limits only what `status --next` proposes. A feedback-reflow repair and an
FO fix authorized under Review-finding disposition step 3 are dispatched at once in the
entity's own worktree, after the existing overlap check against running worktrees; they
do not wait for another entity's worker in the same stage. The validation recheck of
that repair or fix does not wait for another entity's worker either, but it is
dispatched only after the repair or fix has completed and committed its candidate, so
the validator reads the bytes that will be delivered. A repair that outgrows what its
assignment names returns to FO as a scope change.

FO resolves `<package>` in this workflow from the `Package root:` line of
`kc-dev-flow-2:dev`. Before each worker dispatch FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/package_version.py
<this README>`; exit 1 means the session loaded an older package than this README was synced
from, and FO holds the dispatch until the session runs the newer one. FO also runs
`python3 <package>/scripts/workflow_checkout.py <this README>`, which compares this file with
`origin/<trunk>`'s: exit 1 means they differ, exit 2 that it could not compare, and FO
holds the dispatch and shows the Captain what the script printed. Every worker dispatch FO builds carries that absolute path as a
`Package root: <absolute path>` line in its scope notes (`--scope-notes-file`), which
land in the dispatch file the worker reads first. Those scope notes, and every follow-up
message to a live worker, also carry ``Send your completion message to `main` (the README's Dispatch
facts: `team-lead` is not registered here).``: the builder's completion block names `team-lead`, and a
worker that skips the stage-definition fetch does not see the Signal fact. FO saves those scope notes, the
checklist, the model it dispatches on and the SHA it dispatches from as
`<task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md` in the state checkout (for validation a
`Candidate: <full head SHA>` line per head validated),
committed with that dispatch's `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, so
the instruction a worker followed outlives the session that wrote it; FO runs
`python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py <task folder>` before committing and fixes each part it lists. A follow-up
message to a worker FO resumes is a dispatch too, with the same check and a checklist of the items that message asks, never a pointer to another record.
A checklist or scope-notes line that names a package script writes
`<package>/scripts/NAME.py` with the absolute root substituted, never the bare script
name; before `dispatch build`, FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py --names <record>`
on the saved record and rewrites each name it lists. When `status --set` refuses to leave a stage, run `spacedock status --workflow-dir
<dir> --read <task> --stage <stage> --checklist`, return any line it reports as neither
DONE nor SKIPPED to the worker, and do not edit the worker's report. The refusal itself
does not say why; other causes are a missing evidence line or Summary and an uncommitted
report.

### `backlog`

The user selects the compatible profile and approves outcome, scope and budget.
FO records the choice; this boundary has no worker or placeholder report. FO
- **Package:** `<package>` in stage text is the `Package root:` line of the
  kc-dev-flow-2 skill you loaded; your dispatch's scope notes state the same path,
  and if they differ, use the skill's. Run package scripts only from it; never
  search the filesystem, `/tmp` or another install for them.
- **Secrets:** `<wrapper>` is the only route to a development secret: run a
  command that needs one as `<wrapper> <command>`. Never read or print a value.
  If a guard refuses a command that only mentions a secret-reading tool, rephrase

## Review-finding disposition

Before repair authorization, product bytes and the recorded candidate revision stay
unchanged. Read-only inspection, non-mutating reproductions, existing tests and
throwaway-checkout probes are allowed. Report/gate commits may advance repository
HEAD without changing the candidate. Validators recommend `PASSED` or `REJECTED`;
new findings or changed evidence re-enter this checkpoint.

The four evidence fields are released user and normal workflow; observable harm;
affected value acceptance criterion or non-negotiable boundary; and trigger
evidence. Field 3 uses `value-ac[AC-N]`, `captain-ruling[YYYY-MM-DD]`, or
`contract[repo/relative/path#anchor]` plus a nonblank claim. `none:` with a rationale
does not establish Material.

- **Material:** all four fields establish supported-workflow harm to a protected
  boundary or value acceptance criterion.
- **Deferred risk:** hypothetical, unsupported, unobserved or unpromised trigger;
  record what would make it material.
- **Polish:** no current user-visible loss or protected boundary is at risk.
- **Needs decision:** the task cannot own the scope, product or compatibility call.

A `Follow-up:` line in Scope is not accepted scope by itself: the first stage of the
receiving task to meet it assesses it against its stated reason and earlier rulings. It builds the line only when the change alters no behaviour that an
accepted criterion, a Captain ruling or a journey contract relies on; otherwise it
returns the line to FO as a Needs decision. It records which, and why.
A finding FO declined in a committed gate summary or under `### FO declines` is settled:
a later validator does not report it again unless the candidate changes the lines or the
evidence the decline names, or new evidence would make it Material.

## FO steps: review findings

Apply this checkpoint to findings from implementation, validation, detached audits,
consequential FO quick work and rejected gates.

1. Reviewers observe; workers' classifications and `actor:ensign` Resolutions are
   advisory. Preserve findings and assess the four evidence fields above, separating
   materiality, ownership and disposition. Missing required evidence or unresolved
   classification requires investigation or hold.
2. Within approved boundaries, FO may explicitly decline evidenced Deferred risk or
   Polish in the existing committed gate summary, naming the finding, reason, candidate
   revision and the lines or evidence it rests on. When that summary is already
   consumed, FO writes the decline under `### FO declines` in the task file, committed
   with `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, and the terminal gate
   lists each entry there. This FO-authored decision requires no live worker or reviewer
   rerun for acknowledgement; preserve worker reports and verdicts.
3. Repairs require worker investigation without candidate mutation, distinct FO
   `fix` authorization through the runtime's addressable-worker boundary, then
   independent validation. Without that authorization, hold.
4. Scope, value, threshold, tolerance, risk-acceptance and acceptance-criteria
   changes require the Captain. Material findings cannot use the record-only lane;
   hold/route-for-decision forbids repair and reviewer rerun.
5. A round is one verdict of an external reviewer of the delivery on the PR head (Codex
   on the PR, RoboRev or another); FO counts rounds and records the count in the
   committed gate summary. A reviewer that a listed extension covers is read the way its
   `EXTENSION.md` says (`## Extensions`). A finding assessed Material, or labelled P1 by
   the reviewer, blocks in every round: a reviewer P1 is fixed and revalidated, or
   waived by the Captain with the reason recorded (step 4). For an external reviewer
   that has no P1 label, its highest severity level counts as P1 (e.g. RoboRev). Rounds
   1 and 2 follow steps 1 to 4. From round 3 a finding that is neither does not start a
   repair cycle: FO declines it in the committed gate summary, naming the finding, and
   files it as a new backlog task with `spacedock new` whose body carries the finding
   and the decline reason, or names the backlog task that already holds it when a later
   round repeats it; it never enters an open task's Scope. The terminal gate lists each
   such task.

Rejection routing carries evidence, classifications, authorized dispositions and assignment
without re-triage.

Materiality and ownership are independent. Owned Material is eligible for an
FO-authorized fix; out-of-scope Material holds as Needs decision. Deferred risk
or Polish may use the recorded FO decline above within existing risk acceptance.

A Needs decision put to the Captain at a gate carries FO's recommendation. His
plain approval accepts that recommendation only when the gate question says so,
for example "approving accepts the recommendation for D2; say if you object".
Without that sentence a decision he did not address stays open: FO records its
handling as FO's reading, never as his ruling, and asks him.

A decision an accepted ADR already settles is not asked again: FO applies it and states it
in the gate summary as `Precedent: ADR <number> — 「<that ADR's Words line>」`, and the
Captain may reopen it. An ADR with no Words line is quoted by the decision sentence it
applies, as `Precedent: ADR <number> (no Words line) — 「<that sentence>」`. Authority, a gate approval, a merge, an outward-facing action, an
irreversible change and money are always asked, whatever an ADR says, and an ADR on one
of them is never a `Precedent:` line.

A Captain ruling is his reply to the question it settles, given after that question
was put. FO never records as his ruling: silence on a decision the question did not
state approval accepts, consent he gave earlier to a different question, or a choice
he raised but did not make. FO answers a question the Captain asks at a gate before
dispatching on it, and returns a choice he raised to him rather than to a worker.

When the Captain chooses differently from the recommendation, FO writes
`Override: recommended <option>; Captain chose <option>; area: <area>` in the gate
resolution reason, so later workers find past rulings with `git grep 'Override:'` in
the state checkout.

## Decision records

The implementation worker writes one ADR file per decision by its stage principles.
Validation runs `python3 <package>/scripts/adr_lint.py docs/adr --since <base>`, which
requires every record the candidate added or changed, plus `--require <numbers>` for
each `ADR:` number the task's `## Number guards` reserves and any number the
implementation report names; exit 1 or a missing record returns through the existing
feedback route, and exit 2 is a configuration error that returns to FO.

## FO steps: decision records

A ruling settled at a gate, in a worker report, or mid-stage feedback — a rule about
the product, a constraint, or a direction later work must respect — is landed as an
ADR before the next gate is presented, at latest by the terminal approval. A ruling
that governs only this task's own work stays in the task. A design names an ADR
by its ruling and the file's short title, with no number; FO reserves the number when
it dispatches implementation (Number guards) and the implementation worker writes
`docs/adr/<reserved number>-<short-title>.md`. FO confirms the validation ADR lint
passes before presenting the gate. A deferred user-facing capability belongs on
the product's journey map, not here.

## Captain amendments

A change the Captain makes to what he has accepted, whether at a gate approval,
during implementation or at a validation gate, is an amendment. A change he asks for
while the gate that would accept it is still open is not one: he calls `revise`; at a stage
with no `feedback-to` that dispatches a worker, that stage's worker reworks it; at a stage
whose gate has a `feedback-to`, the revision goes to that target and the stage's worker
re-reviews it; and at `backlog`, which dispatches no worker, FO revises the recorded outcome,
scope or budget, or asks the proposal's author to.

FO appends one entry per amendment to the task's `## Captain amendments` section and
changes nothing else in it. FO adds no words of its own and does not move or rewrite a criterion:

```
## Captain amendments

### Amendment 1 — <date>, <gate or chat>
Captain: 「<his words, verbatim>」 (where he said them)
Asked: <the question or proposal he answered, verbatim, or the commit holding it>
Supersedes: <acceptance-criterion ids, or none> <optional: "(no replacement: <why>)">
Design: <optional: the design paragraph it overrides>
```

`Asked:` is required when his words do not name what they settle, such as 「同意第三點」. FO
names the amendment in the next dispatch's checklist. That worker (implementation, the
repair worker on a feedback route, or the worker of the stage a task is sent back to)
moves each superseded criterion's block verbatim from `## Acceptance criteria` into its
entry under a `Superseded text:` line, writes any replacement as a new `**AC-N**` under
a fresh id that says "Amended by Captain, amendment N", and never reuses an id. A
superseded criterion and the design paragraph named by `Design:` are withdrawn; evidence
and the Captain's acceptance script follow `## Acceptance criteria` plus the entries.

Sending an approved task back to an earlier stage, such as a design redo a release
review asks for, is the Captain's decision and is recorded as an amendment whose
`Design:` names what is redone; FO then runs `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir>
--set <slug> status=<stage>`, and that stage's gate is approved again before the task
moves on.

`python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check <task>`, run by implementation and
validation, prints each defect and exits 1; repair findings return through feedback. It cannot see a skipped record or
move, or FO's words in `Design:`.

## Affected documents

Implementation runs `python3 <package>/scripts/doc_impact.py <base> <candidate>`
and records, for each listed document, `updated` or `unaffected: <reason>` in its
stage report; validation reruns it at the candidate and checks every listed

the package's `references/retained-documents.md`.

## Number guards

Applies when the task's `Surfaces:` includes `db`, or the task lands an ADR, including one first required by a ruling in a worker report or mid-stage feedback, whose number FO reserves before the next dispatch; the POC bullet below applies to every `poc` task.

def bare_names(text, names):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    if not any(SCANNED.match(line) for line in lines):
        scanned = range(len(lines))
    else:
        scanned, inside = [], False
        for number, line in enumerate(lines):
            if line.startswith("## "):
                inside = bool(SCANNED.match(line))
            elif inside:
                scanned.append(number)
    return [(number + 1, name) for number in scanned
            for name in dict.fromkeys(SCRIPT_TOKEN.findall(lines[number])) if name in names]


def check_names(files, package):
    names = package_scripts(package)
    found = False
    for file in files:
        for number, name in bare_names(Path(file).read_text(), names):
            print(f"{file}:{number}: bare package script name {name}")
            found = True
    return 1 if found else 0


def check_candidates(files):
    found = False
    for file in files:
        path = Path(file).resolve()
        if path.parent.name != "dispatch" or not RECORD.match(path.name):
            continue
        header = re.split(r"^## ", path.read_text(), maxsplit=1, flags=re.M)[0]
        if not CANDIDATE.search(header):
            print(f"{file}:1: no 'Candidate: <40-hex head>' line; add one per head to validate above the first '## ' heading, "
                  "then run this check again")
            found = True
    return 1 if found else 0


def check_newest(state, slug, package):
    done = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(state), "log", "--diff-filter=A", "--no-renames", "--relative",
                           "--name-only", "--format=", "-n", "1", "--", f"{slug}/dispatch/"],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    if done.returncode:
        print(f"git cannot read the dispatch records: {' '.join(done.stderr.split())}")
        return 2
    added = sorted(line for line in done.stdout.splitlines() if line.endswith(".md"))
    record = Path(state, added[-1]) if added else None
    return check_names([record], package) if record and record.is_file() else 0


def main(argv=None, package=PACKAGE):
    args = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    if args[:1] == ["--names"] and len(args) > 1:
        return max(check_names(args[1:], package), check_candidates(args[1:]))
    if args[:1] == ["--newest"] and len(args) == 3:
        return check_newest(args[1], args[2], package)
    readme = None
    if "--readme" in args:
        at = args.index("--readme")
        given, args = args[at + 1:at + 2], args[:at] + args[at + 2:]
        if not given:
            print(__doc__.strip())
            return 2
        readme = Path(given[0])
        if not readme.is_file():
            print(f"--readme {readme}: no such file")
            return 2
    if len(args) != 1 or args[0] in ("--names", "--newest"):
        print(__doc__.strip())
        return 2
    task = Path(args[0])
    folder = task.with_suffix("") if task.suffix == ".md" else task
    records = sorted((folder / "dispatch").glob("*.md"))
    if not records:
        print(f"{folder}: no dispatch records under dispatch/")
        return 1
    errors = [f"{path.name}: needs {part}" for path in records
              for part, pattern in PARTS.items() if not pattern.search(path.read_text())]
    readme = readme or find_readme(folder)
    if readme:
        errors += extension_errors(folder, readme, package)
    names = [path.stem for path in records]
    for path in records:
        if only_points_at_records(path.read_text(), [name for name in names if name != path.stem]):
            errors.append(f"{path.name}: needs a checklist of its own, not only a reference to another dispatch record")
    for error in errors:
        print(error)
    if not readme:
        print(f"extensions not checked: no workflow README above {folder}")
    if not errors:
        print(f"{len(records)} dispatch record(s) complete")
    return 1 if errors else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def fix_gaps(texts):
    def text(fix):
        return texts[fix.get("file", "references/sd/workflow.md")]
    return {name: ([p for p in fix["need"] if p not in text(fix)], [p for p in fix["old"] if p in text(fix)])
            for name, fix in FIXES.items()}


def at_0_10_1(texts, name):
    path = FIXES[name].get("file", "references/sd/workflow.md")
    flat = texts[path]
    for pattern, old in FIXES[name]["swaps"]:
        flat, count = re.subn(pattern, lambda _: old, flat)
        assert count == 1, (name, pattern, count)
    return {**texts, path: flat}


def exercise(base, binary, sd_root):
    token = uuid.uuid4().hex[:10]
    artifacts = []
    env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items()
           if key not in ("GIT_DIR", "GIT_WORK_TREE", "GIT_INDEX_FILE")}
    env["SPACEDOCK_BIN"] = binary

    def run(args, cwd=base, data=None, expected=0, child_env=None):
        call_env = env if child_env is None else child_env
        result = subprocess.run([str(arg) for arg in args], cwd=cwd, env=call_env,
                                input=data, text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=30)
        with (base / "commands.jsonl").open("a") as log:
            log.write(json.dumps({"argv": [str(arg) for arg in args], "cwd": str(cwd),
                                  "stdin": data, "exit": result.returncode,
                                  "runtime_markers": [key for key in ("CLAUDECODE", "CODEX_THREAD_ID", "PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR") if call_env.get(key)],
                                  "stdout": result.stdout, "stderr": result.stderr}) + "\n")
        if expected is not None and result.returncode != expected:
            raise AssertionError(f"{args}: exit {result.returncode}\n{result.stderr}")
        return result

    def route_definition(profile):
        definition = TEMPLATE.read_text()
        if profile == "poc":
            definition = re.sub(r"    - name: ideation\n.*?(?=    - name: implementation)", "", definition, flags=re.DOTALL)
            definition = re.sub(r"### `ideation`\n.*?(?=### `implementation`)", "", definition, flags=re.DOTALL)
        return definition

    def seed(name, stage, definition=None, profile="pilot", with_mod=True):
        repo = base / name
        repo.mkdir()
        workflow = repo / "docs" / ("dev2-poc" if profile == "poc" else "dev2")
        workflow.mkdir(parents=True)
        (workflow / "README.md").write_text(definition or route_definition(profile))
        (repo / ".gitignore").write_text(".worktrees/\n**/.spacedock-state/\n")
        if with_mod:
            (workflow / "_mods").mkdir()
            shutil.copyfile(sd_root / "mods/pr-merge.md", workflow / "_mods/pr-merge.md")
        run(["git", "init", "--initial-branch=main", repo])
        for key, value in (("user.name", "Dev Flow Fixture"), ("user.email", "fixture@example.invalid"),
                           ("commit.gpgsign", "false"), ("core.hooksPath", "/dev/null")):
            run(["git", "-C", repo, "config", key, value])
        files = [".gitignore", str((workflow / "README.md").relative_to(repo))]
        if with_mod:
            files.append(str((workflow / "_mods/pr-merge.md").relative_to(repo)))
        run(["git", "-C", repo, "add", "--", *files])
        run(["git", "-C", repo, "commit", "-m", "test: seed synthetic CLI workflow"])
        # Commission's orphan-state journey, confined to this disposable repository.
        state = workflow / ".spacedock-state"
        run(["git", "-C", repo, "worktree", "add", "--detach", state])
        run(["git", "-C", state, "checkout", "--orphan", f"spacedock-state/{workflow.name}"])
        run(["git", "-C", state, "rm", "-rf", "."])
        slug = f"df2-{token}-{name}"
        entity = state / f"{slug}.md"
        template = TEMPLATE.read_text().split("```markdown\n", 1)[1].split("```", 1)[0]
        entity.write_text(template.replace("<task-id>", slug).replace("<selected-profile>", profile)
                          .replace("<bounded outcome>", "Synthetic CLI fixture, not product acceptance")
                          .replace("status: backlog", f"status: {stage}"))
        run(["git", "-C", state, "add", "--", entity.name])
        run(["git", "-C", state, "commit", "-m", "test: seed synthetic task state"])
        return workflow, entity

    def request(repo, entity, stage, host):
        return {"schema_version": 2, "entity_path": str(entity), "workflow_dir": str(repo),
                "stage": stage, "host": host, "checklist": ["Inspect the selected stage boundary"]}

    def snapshot(repo, entity):
        return (entity.read_bytes(), run(["git", "-C", repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD"]).stdout,
                run(["git", "-C", repo, "status", "--porcelain=v1", "--untracked-files=all"]).stdout)

    try:
        version = run([binary, "--version"]).stdout.splitlines()[0]
        for stage in STAGES:
            for host in ("claude", "codex"):
                repo, entity = seed(f"{host}-{stage}", stage)
                payload = request(repo, entity, stage, host)
                payload_path = base / f"{host}-{stage}.json"
                payload_path.write_text(json.dumps(payload))
                checklist_path = base / "transport-checklist.txt"
                checklist_path.write_text("Synthetic dispatch only; no worker execution\n")
                notes_path = base / "transport-scope-notes.txt"
                package_root = ROOT
                notes_path.write_text(f"Package root: {package_root}\n"
                                      f"{MAIN_LINE}\n"
                                      f"Run {package_root}/scripts/comment_ratio.py from the base to HEAD.\n")
                result = run([binary, "dispatch", "build", "--workflow-dir", repo,
                              "--entity-path", entity, "--stage", stage, "--host", host,
                              "--checklist-file", checklist_path, "--scope-notes-file", notes_path,
                              "--stamp"], repo)
                run([binary, "dispatch", "build", "--validate-only", payload_path], repo)
                envelope = json.loads(result.stdout)
                artifact = Path(envelope["dispatch_file_path"])
                if token not in artifact.name:
                    raise AssertionError("unexpected dispatch artifact ownership")
                artifacts.append(artifact)
                body = artifact.read_text()
                (base / f"{host}-{stage}-dispatch.md").write_text(body)
                assert str(entity) in body and f"Stage: {stage}" in body
                assert str(artifact) in envelope["prompt"]
                assert envelope["subagent_type"] == "spacedock:ensign"
                bootstrap = 'Skill(skill="spacedock:ensign")' if host == "claude" else "$spacedock:ensign"

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--keep", action="store_true", help="keep successful fixture repos and raw CLI evidence")
    parser.add_argument("--sd-plugin-root", type=Path, required=True,
                        help="activated SD plugin root supplying unmodified mods/pr-merge.md")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not (args.sd_plugin_root / "mods/pr-merge.md").is_file():
        parser.error("--sd-plugin-root must contain the activated mods/pr-merge.md")
    binary = shutil.which(os.environ.get("SPACEDOCK_BIN") or "spacedock")
    if not binary:
        parser.error("set SPACEDOCK_BIN to the installed Spacedock executable")
    base = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="dev-flow-2-sd-")).resolve()
    try:
        exercise(base, str(Path(binary).resolve()), args.sd_plugin_root.resolve())
    except Exception:
        print(f"FAIL: fixtures and raw CLI evidence retained at {base}")
        raise
    if args.keep:
        print(f"Evidence: {base}")
    else:
        shutil.rmtree(base)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Adopt the SD workflow

Use this reference from `kc-dev-flow-2:dev` when adoption is absent or incompatible.
Invoke `spacedock:commission` for a new workflow, or `spacedock:refit` to review an
existing one. This reference supplies design inputs, not an alternate setup CLI.
Reuse the user's established selection; obtain approval for concrete configuration
changes before activating dispatch. Do not run commission's pilot automatically
as part of installing this package.

## Resolve and propose

Resolve the absolute code root, target workflow directory, installed dev2 package,
activated SD plugin root and executable version. Read project conventions, live
workflows, task ownership and delivery authority. Existing work remains on its
recorded workflow/variant/profile. A profile change requires a reviewed route
and migration decision; do not move tasks or overwrite custom mods implicitly.

Use the [workflow source](workflow.md) as the commission input. SD advances along
ordered stage definitions; a profile field does not branch that graph. Adopt only
the route currently needed:

| Selected profile | Workflow directory example | Source adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `poc` | `docs/dev2-poc` | Generated, never hand-edited: `<package>/scripts/poc_readme.py derive` removes the ideation state entry and the `### ideation` section; backlog, implementation, validation and done stay byte-identical |
| `pilot` or `prod` | `docs/dev2` | Keep the source's five stages; profile selects skill references per task |

Maintain one README by hand. When both routes are adopted, commission or refit the
five-stage README first, then regenerate the POC README from it:
`python3 <package>/scripts/poc_readme.py derive docs/dev2/README.md > docs/dev2-poc/README.md`.
When only POC is adopted, derive from this package's [workflow source](workflow.md)
and resolve its template values the same way. After any change to the five-stage
README, regenerate; `python3 <package>/scripts/poc_readme.py check docs/dev2-poc/README.md docs/dev2/README.md`
exits 1 with the drift as a diff.

Both routes preserve backlog/validation gates, implementation/validation
`worktree: true`, fresh validation and `feedback-to: implementation`. Copy the
source into the approved workflow's `README.md`, resolve template values
(including `<wrapper>`, below) and project trunk and ID policy, and stamp
commissioning metadata through SD's existing procedure. The source uses slug IDs; commission may propose its collaborative
SD-B32 ID policy. Preserve an existing workflow's approved ID style.
Stage prose calls exact `kc-dev-flow-2:` skills; `context-sections` lists only the
sections a stage's worker acts on (dispatch facts, the classification vocabulary, decision
records, amendments, affected documents, number guards). The FO steps for finding
disposition, decision records and number guards, and delivery authority, are sections no
worker receives. Do not introduce unsupported `stage.skill` fields or
profile-conditioned transitions. Check profile/graph compatibility before new
work or resume dispatch; a mismatch holds the affected action for the user.

## State and delivery setup

Use commission's split-root journey for a shipping code repository: state stays
in the workflow's ignored `.spacedock-state` linked checkout, code changes in the
task worktree, and the workflow README/mods on the code branch. Choose distinct
workflow basenames and state branches (`spacedock-state/dev2-poc` versus
`spacedock-state/dev2` above); inspect existing branches before creating anything.
Keep both state paths and `.worktrees/` ignored. Preserve existing state layout
unless an explicit migration is approved. Pass the absolute workflow directory
to `spacedock state init`/`ready`, status, gate, dispatch and merge operations.

For PR delivery, have commission install `{active-sd-root}/mods/pr-merge.md` into
`{workflow-dir}/_mods/pr-merge.md`. Copy the activated source unchanged, not a
vendored dev2 copy or an arbitrary cache version. Record/check its own metadata
and bytes; mod version and plugin version need not match (the inspected SD 0.27.3
package ships pr-merge 0.27.0). Refit compares existing customizations for approval.
The workflow's Delivery authority constrains the upstream mod's local fallback,
trunk push and non-Draft defaults. Preserve project Draft/CI/manual merge rules;
installing the mod does not grant those actions or mechanically enforce them.

The package also owns `<package>/references/sd/mods/kc-dev-flow-2.md`. In the change that
re-syncs a workflow README (here `docs/dev2` and `docs/dev2-poc`), copy it into
`{workflow-dir}/_mods/`, run `cmp` against the package copy, and check that
`spacedock status --workflow-dir {workflow-dir} --boot` lists `kc-dev-flow-2` before `pr-merge`
on its `idle:` and `startup:` lines and `pr-merge` alone on `merge:`.

## Comment ratio and review rounds

`<package>/scripts/comment_ratio.py` fails a candidate whose added comments exceed
5 percent of its added code lines (the package default, once at least 20 code
lines are added) or that cite task numbering, review provenance, a PR or issue
number or a `file:line`. An adopter sets its own value with
`comment-ratio-max: <percent>` in its workflow README frontmatter; `--max` overrides
both for one run. The citation scan is a pattern list: it also flags a `#333` colour,
`step #1`, a URL fragment, an asyncio "Task 3", "a code review of the parser" and
"the Codex CLI" (1 false positive in 38 hits on the last 150 commits of the package
repository's main); reword such a comment. The review-round rule and the repair
lane live in `workflow.md`: an adopter that already has a workflow README receives
them by re-syncing that README from `workflow.md`, a per-adopter three-way merge that keeps its own
frontmatter; the package does not rewrite an adopter's README. Update the plugin before
re-syncing a README: worker rules also copied into the skills' `principles.md` arrive with
the plugin, so once the workflow copy is removed a README re-synced first leaves those
workers without them. The re-sync must take the new `context-sections` lists together with
the section text. The merge keeps the adopter's frontmatter, so an old list keeps
delivering FO-only text such as Delivery authority to workers, and a list naming a section
the README lacks makes Spacedock refuse every dispatch.

## Ideation checks and Captain amendments

The FO steps (the backlog seed check, the amendment record, ADR number reservation at
implementation dispatch) live in `workflow.md`: an adopter receives them by re-syncing
its workflow README from `workflow.md`, the same per-adopter three-way merge as above.
The amendment rule a worker follows (record format, move duty, run-`check` clause) reaches it
the same way, through that re-sync, not with the package; the ideation worker rules and
`<package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py` arrive with the package. Until the README is
re-synced, the adopter's FO does not run the seed check and its workers do not see the
amendment rule.

## State laws check

`<package>/references/sd/laws.md` lists the laws and `<package>/scripts/laws_check.py` checks them over the
committed state-branch history. `<package>/references/sd/state-laws.workflow.yml` runs it on each push to one
named state branch. Each run judges only the events the commits of that push add, the `before..after` range
GitHub reports, so there are no anchors to set: adopting starts green, because the first range holds the
one commit that adds the workflow file. A violation is reported once, in the run of the push that added it;
the next push is judged on its own commits, so its run is green again whether or not the violation was
repaired. A failed run reaches the pushing account as GitHub's failed-run notice, which is the whole signal.
A push the runner cannot read (a new branch, a force push whose old head is gone, a shallow clone) is a red
run that says `cannot judge`. To audit old history once, run the same command by hand with `--before` set to
the root commit; it reports old violations and gates nothing. The run detects after the push; it does not stop
`merge guard`, a dispatch or a push, and it adds no word to what FO reads.

Roll it out once per adopter, on the Captain's word: FO copies the template to `.github/workflows/dev2-laws.yml`
on the state branch with the branch name, trunk workflow directory and a package commit that a
published `kc-dev-flow-2-vX.Y.Z` tag points at, and commits that one path with a path-scoped `git add` and
`git commit -- <path>`, then pushes. A workflow whose state is inline in trunk has no state branch to trigger on.

Verified on a throwaway branch of this repository's state branch: GitHub runs a push workflow committed on that
branch, hands it `github.event.before` and `github.event.after`, and runs one workflow per push. Not
verified: the minutes a private adopter pays per run, and `spacedock state init`, `gate prepare`, `gate record`
and `merge guard --rework` leaving a committed `.github/` file unchanged on this release.

# Observer

Invocation: `kc-dev-flow-2:observer`

Package root: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}
`<package>` in this skill is this root. If the value above is not an absolute path,
the root is two directories above this `SKILL.md`.

Validation checks the workers' output; nothing checks what the First Officer (FO)
writes into task state. You read those writes as someone who was not there. The caller
supplies only these inputs, never its own account of the task:

- `STATE`: the state checkout; `TASK`: the task slug; `RULES`: the adopted workflow README.
- `FROM` and `TO`: state commits bounding the window. When not given, `FROM` is the
  commit that added the task file and `TO` is the state checkout's `HEAD`.

## Read

1. `git -C STATE log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=iso FROM..TO -- <task file> <task dir>`
   and the diff over the same range. Read the task at `TO` only around changed hunks. For an
   archived task give git both path pairs, `<TASK>.md <TASK>` and `_archive/<TASK>.md
   _archive/<TASK>`, and take `FROM` from the commit that added `<TASK>.md`; the archive
   commit alone leaves a window of one commit.
2. `python3 <package>/scripts/decision_ledger.py STATE`, keeping the rows for `TASK`:
   each gate ruling with its question, who recorded it, its grant and any `Override:`.
3. From RULES collect every sentence whose subject is FO ("FO records", "FO appends",
   "FO declines", "FO reserves", "FO names", "FO counts", "FO applies") and that applied
   in this window. Quote each with its section heading.

Check at least: a Captain ruling quotes his words and answers a question put before it;
an approval read as accepting a recommendation has that sentence in its question; a
decision by `agent:first-officer` carries the grant it relies on; an `Override:` line
exists where his choice differs from the stated recommendation; a `Precedent:` names an
ADR and quotes its Words line, or its decision sentence when marked `(no Words line)`,
and is not one of the always-asked kinds; amendments and
`Asked:` lines follow `## Captain amendments`; declines follow step 5 of review findings.
Where RULES list `peers` under `extensions:`, also check that no Captain ruling in the task
quotes a peer's words, or a peer's report of the Captain, in place of his own; a ruling he
made in his own words after reading peer data is his. An exchange the file does not record
is outside what state shows.

For a task whose `Surfaces:` include `db`, whose ideation ran on a stronger model, or
whose validation was sent back twice, report whether a `Reviewer:` line exists. That
line is a record, not a requirement: report it as `observed`, never as a violation.
Separately, run `python3 <package>/scripts/role_triggers.py STATE TASK --rev TO` and report each
`next:` line it prints as `violation`, quoting that line.

## Prove each finding

Before reporting a finding, find its evidence quote with `git -C STATE show TO:<path>`,
`git grep` or the ledger output, and drop it if the quote is not there. A rule that did
not apply in the window is not listed. Decide the verdict word last, from the evidence
you wrote.

## Return (under 500 words)

One line per finding:
`<violation|ok|can't tell|observed> | rule: "<quoted rule>" (<section>) | evidence: "<quoted line or 'absent'>" (<commit>)`

`can't tell` names the evidence that is outside state (chat, a PR, a database).
Then `Coverage:` what you read fully, what you sampled, and each rule you could not
evaluate.

## Boundaries

Read-only: no edit, commit, push, comment or message. Do not judge product content,
design quality or worker reports, and do not propose a repair. The caller passes the
report on unedited; whoever owns the task answers it.

def frontmatter(readme):
    if not readme.is_file():
        raise Misconfigured(f"no workflow README at {readme}")
    lines = readme.read_text().split("\n")
    found = {}
    for line in lines[1:] if lines[0] == "---" else []:
        if line == "---":
            break
        match = re.match(r"^([\w-]+):[ \t]*(.*?)[ \t]*$", line)
        if match:
            found[match.group(1)] = match.group(2).strip("'\"")
    return found


def task_facts(path):
    task = Path(path)
    if not task.is_file():
        raise Misconfigured(f"task file {task} does not exist")
    text = task.read_text(errors="replace")
    section = re.search(r"^## Number guards[ \t]*\n(.*?)(?=^## |\Z)", text, re.M | re.S)
    body = section.group(1) if section else ""
    surfaces = re.search(r"^Surfaces:(.*)$", text, re.M)
    return {
        "migration": {int(n) for n in re.findall(r"^Migration:[ \t]*(\d+)[ \t]*$", body, re.M)},
        "adr": {int(n) for n in re.findall(r"^ADR:[ \t]*(\d+)[ \t]*$", body, re.M)},
        "applied": re.findall(r"^Applied at:[ \t]*(\S+)[ \t]+([0-9a-f]{7,40})[ \t]*$", body, re.M),
        "poc": frontmatter(task).get("profile") == "poc",
        "surfaces": set(re.split(r"[\s,]+", surfaces.group(1).strip())) if surfaces else set(),
    }


def numbered(repo, ref, directory, pattern):
    found = {}
    for path in git(repo, "ls-tree", "--name-only", ref, directory.rstrip("/") + "/").splitlines():
        match = pattern.match(posixpath.basename(path))
        if match:
            found.setdefault(int(match.group(1)), []).append(posixpath.basename(path))
    return found


def added_changed(repo, old, new, directory, pattern):
    """Return (added files, files present at old and modified or deleted at new) among numbered files in directory."""
    added, touched = [], []
    out = git(repo, "diff", "--name-status", "--no-renames", old, new, "--", directory.rstrip("/") + "/")
    for line in out.splitlines():
        status, path = line.split("\t", 1)
        if posixpath.dirname(path) != directory.rstrip("/") or not pattern.match(posixpath.basename(path)):
            continue
        (added if status == "A" else touched).append((status, path))
    return added, touched


def settings(args):
    cfg = frontmatter(Path(args.workflow_dir) / "README.md") if args.workflow_dir else {}
    base = args.base
    if not base and cfg.get("trunk"):
        remote = f"origin/{cfg['trunk']}"
        base = remote if subprocess.run(["git", "-C", args.repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", remote],
                                        capture_output=True).returncode == 0 else cfg["trunk"]
    if not base:
        raise Misconfigured("no base: pass --base, or --workflow-dir whose README declares trunk:")
    return {
        "migrations": args.migrations_path or cfg.get("migrations-path"),
        "adr": args.adr_path or cfg.get("adr-path") or "docs/adr",
        "base": base,
        "state": getattr(args, "state_dir", None) or (cfg.get("state") and str(Path(args.workflow_dir) / cfg["state"])),
    }
